alert: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat or difficulty breathing: call emergency services immediately. Chronic hives are treated with antihistamines.
lifex: A diary of possible triggers (heat, pressure, stress)

alert: Severe dry, itchy skin may be linked to the thyroid, kidneys or eczema.
A new dark spot that changes shape or colour needs a dermatologist.
avoid: Perfume on the skin in the sun
lifex: Broad-spectrum sunscreen every day, even when cloudy

alert: High fever, shortness of breath or a cough lasting more than 3 weeks needs a doctor to rule out pneumonia. Antibiotics usually do not help.
lifex: Honey for the cough (not for babies)

alert: In babies, with high fever, swelling behind the ear or fluid from the ear, see a doctor. Many ear infections clear on their own in 2–3 days.
avoid: Herbal ear drops if there is discharge
lifex: Breastfeeding and no smoking at home

alert: Leg weakness, numbness around the genitals or loss of bladder or bowel control: go to hospital immediately.
diff: Without pain running down the leg

alert: Left shoulder pain with chest pain or breathlessness: call emergency services. Frozen shoulder is more common in diabetes.
Sudden hip pain after a fall in an older person may be a fracture.
Very heavy periods, dizziness or pain need a gynaecologist. Anaemia is common.
avoid: High doses of green tea extract without a doctor
why_v: Low levels linked with larger fibroids, small studies
If there is anaemia from heavy periods
One small study, only with a doctor because of the liver

alert: Bleeding after menopause needs a gynaecologist. Local oestrogen is safe and very effective.
More than 3 months without a period (when not pregnant) needs a gynaecologist. Take a pregnancy test.
lifex: Weight loss if there is obesity

alert: A lump you can feel, or changes in the nipple or skin, need a doctor.
avoid: Reported to worsen it, weak data

alert: Weight gain of more than 2 kg in 3 days, breathlessness when lying down or swelling: contact your cardiologist promptly.
why_v: Fewer hospital admissions in one trial (Q-SYMBIO)
Intravenous iron for deficiency, only from a cardiologist

alert: Very high values need checking for B12 or folate deficiency, kidney disease or an inherited cause.
avoid: Lowering it did not prevent heart attacks in trials

alert: This is not a recognised diagnosis. True adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) is serious: weakness, weight loss, low blood pressure and darkened skin need a doctor.
avoid: May contain cortisol or thyroid hormones

alert: Increased permeability occurs in some diseases (coeliac, Crohn's), but it is not a recognised diagnosis on its own. The tests on sale are not reliable.
Diagnosis is difficult and the tests are doubtful. Flushing, headache, diarrhoea or hives after certain foods can have other causes too.
avoid: Very aged cheeses, cured meats, pickles
lifex: Fresh rather than aged foods, with a dietitian

alert: Before cutting out gluten, get tested for coeliac disease. After stopping gluten the test gives a false negative.
avoid: A strict gluten-free diet without reason
Less fibre and fewer B vitamins
diff: Fructans, not gluten, are often to blame
lifex: A low-FODMAP diet with a dietitian

alert: In people on insulin or sulfonylureas, blood sugar under 70 needs 15 g of sugar immediately. Fainting or confusion: call emergency services.
avoid: Sugar and soft drinks on their own
Cause a sharp rise and fall
lifex: Small meals with protein and fibre

alert: Rapid onset, a deepening voice or clitoral enlargement need an urgent endocrine check.
lifex: Weight loss if there is obesity

alert: Unexplained bruises with bleeding gums, nosebleeds or tiny red spots need a blood test. Anticoagulants and aspirin are common causes.

n: Cracks at the corners of the mouth
alert: Often caused by a fungus or bacteria. If it does not clear, see a doctor.
Check B12, folate, iron, blood sugar and medicines. A sore on the tongue that does not heal in 2 weeks needs a doctor.
Twitching with muscle weakness, difficulty swallowing or muscle wasting needs a neurologist. Most twitching is harmless.
avoid: A lot of caffeine and energy drinks

alert: Repeated vomiting, confusion, weakness, seizures or a worsening headache: go to hospital immediately.
avoid: Returning to sport the same day
lifex: A few days of rest and a gradual return

alert: The core support is early intervention (speech, occupational and behavioural therapy). Many online "treatments" are dangerous.
why_v: Folinic acid in a subgroup, only with a doctor

alert: A harmless inherited condition with slightly raised bilirubin. Yellowing with dark urine, pain or fever needs a doctor.
Sudden hearing loss in one ear is urgent: see an ENT doctor within 72 hours.
why_v: One study in people with low folate

alert: Needs regular eye checks. Treatments exist that slow progression (atropine drops, special glasses).
avoid: A lot of close work without breaks
why_v: Linked, but outdoor light seems to be what matters

alert: 6–10 viral infections a year are normal in young children. Difficulty breathing, dehydration or fever lasting more than 3 days need a paediatrician.

n: Child who is short or thin
alert: The paediatrician assesses the growth curve. A slowing growth rate needs checking.
lifex: A varied diet with protein and dairy

alert: No supplement has been shown to prevent cancer. Some increase the risk. Screening tests save lives.
why_v: Perhaps fewer cancer deaths, not fewer diagnoses
Nicotinamide for skin cancer at high risk

alert: Tell your oncologist about every supplement: some interact with tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors.
why_v: For the bones, if diet falls short

alert: Tell your urologist about every supplement. Hormone therapy causes osteoporosis and muscle loss.
why_v: For the bones during hormone therapy

alert: Lp(a) is mainly inherited. One measurement in a lifetime is enough. If it is high, control the other risk factors more strictly.
avoid: Supplements that promise to lower it
lifex: Controlling LDL, blood pressure and blood sugar
why_v: Lowers it, but no benefit on heart attacks and has side effects

alert: Treatments with strong evidence: trauma-focused psychotherapy (e.g. EMDR) and medicines. If you have thoughts of self-harm, contact a crisis line or emergency services immediately.
Common with proton pump inhibitors, diuretics, alcohol and diarrhoea. Very low magnesium causes arrhythmias.
lifex: Nuts, legumes, green vegetables, whole grains

alert: Very low potassium causes weakness and arrhythmias. Replacement with tablets only on medical advice with blood tests.
avoid: Laxatives and diuretics without a doctor
why_v: If magnesium is also low, potassium will not correct

alert: In sarcoidosis vitamin D can raise calcium dangerously. Calcium and vitamin D only on medical advice with blood tests.
In primary hyperparathyroidism calcium is already high: supplements only with an endocrinologist. A common cause of the secondary form is vitamin D deficiency.
why_v: In the secondary form from deficiency, or with caution in the primary form
